gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-noto-sans-arme: A marker-flat line with daylight in every curve marks Red Hat Display. Noto Sans Armenian, a sans-serif, fills the line with full small letters and wide round mouths, while those titles want a few large words.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-noto-sans-bamu: Red Hat Display draws a bold marker line with daylight punched through every curve. And Noto Sans Bamum, a plain sans, holds the running line with unfinished curves and big counters.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-noto-sans-bass: Red Hat Display's marker stroke stays one width, with hollow curves. Noto Sans Bassa Vah, a plain sans, swallows the line's height with an open-jawed c, so display and copy share one high-bodied sheet.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-noto-sans-beng: Capitals barely outgrow the small letters under Red Hat Display's marker line. Noto Sans Bengali, a plain sans, holds the open mouths, while those titles want scale and brevity.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-noto-sans-bhai: Approachable rope-coiled small letters sit under a marker heading from Red Hat Display. Noto Sans Bhaiksuki, a sans-serif, keeps the apertures readable against that cord-cut stroke.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-noto-sans-brah: A technical-pen steadiness, no swell on the curve, marks Red Hat Display, with daylight inside every bend. Noto Sans Brahmi, a sans-serif, still reads a size down, mouths open.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-noto-sans-buhi: Modern gaps between curve and stem sit under Red Hat Display's marker line. And Noto Sans Buhid, a sans-serif, brings a high-set x-height that is the real snap.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-noto-sans-chor: Noto Sans Chorasmian, a sans-serif, stops its curves short and fills the line with a large x-height under Red Hat Display. Drop the body a size; the gaps still show.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-noto-sans-cune: Bent-steel-rod strokes, one width, mark Red Hat Display as bold display. And Noto Sans Cuneiform, a sans-serif, keeps an open e and bead-like small letters through running copy.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-noto-sans-deva: Bold marker titles from Red Hat Display meet a compact, blended skyline. Noto Sans Devanagari, a sans-serif, does the open g and blended caps, while the heading does the tube-like shout.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-noto-sans-elba: Red Hat Display holds a contemporary marker stroke with hollow curves. Noto Sans Elbasan, a plain sans, does the large small letters and un-pinched terminals, while the heading owns the shout.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-noto-sans-elym: Open apertures and stubby ascenders make the body read clean under Red Hat Display. Noto Sans Elymaic, a sans-serif, holds the high-bodied line, while the heading owns the daylight shout.
gen-boska-gf-lexend-giga: Carved-stone stems and scratched-glass serifs, hairline into fat trunks, mark Boska as dramatic. Lexend Giga, a sans, still holds if you drop a size, with wide tracking and stubby ascenders.
gen-fs-chubbo-gf-noto-sans-soyombo: Smooth bends drawn with a marker tip mark Chubbo as casual display. Noto Sans Soyombo, a plain sans, keeps a screen-ready x-height and unclosed mouths through running copy.
gen-fs-chubbo-gf-noto-sans-sunuwar: Casual marker-tip letters from Chubbo invite a smooth path around every bend. And Noto Sans Sunuwar, a plain sans, leaves rope-bight gaps in the curves, while those titles want a few large words.
